title: Closed maximal-rank kernel locus of one finite-free sheaf map
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $M,N$ be structure-sheaf modules, and let $d:M\to N$ be a module-sheaf morphism. Suppose $M\cong\mathcal O_X^{\oplus s}$ and $N\cong\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], where $s,n,r\in\mathbf N$ and $s\le r$. There is a closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], such that for every scheme $T$ and morphism $h:T\to X$, $h$ factors through $i$ if and only if the kernel of the ordinary pulled-back morphism $h^*d:h^*M\to h^*N$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is finite locally free of rank $r$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module].

source.place: local matrix calculation in the proof, using Tag 0EWY; the smaller-domain case uses padding as in the parent node

proof.text: When s=r, choose finite free frames for M and N and form the ideal in Gamma(X,O_X) generated by the finitely many matrix entries. Its quotient spectrum gives a closed subscheme of X. A map factors through it exactly when the pulled-back matrix vanishes. If the kernel is locally free of rank r, trivialize it on affine source neighbourhoods. Its square injective inclusion has cokernel with zero dual by 0EWY, so each coordinate of the map d, which factors through that cokernel, is zero. Conversely the kernel of a zero matrix is the free first term. The local factors agree by monomorphy of the closed immersion.

When s<r, use the empty closed subscheme. On any nonempty affine source neighbourhood, a rank-r kernel would inject into the rank-s first term. Pad the latter with r-s zero coordinates; the resulting square injection has injective transpose by 0EWY, but the transpose annihilates a nonzero padded basis vector. Thus the source must be empty; on the empty source both predicates hold.

The matrix ideal is finitely generated. RingHom.FinitePresentation.of_surjective and LocallyOfFinitePresentation.SpecMap_iff give local finite presentation of its quotient immersion. The empty immersion is likewise finitely presented, using the unit ideal. For s=r=0, the zero matrix cuts out all of X. Empty schemes and zero rings are included.

proof_origin.note: Extracts the ordinary sheaf-map geometry from the parent proof; no complex or derived-category hypothesis.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_affineFreeKernelRankLocus
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X]
    (M N : SheafOfModules.{u} (X.ringCatSheaf)) (d : M ⟶ N)
    (s n r : ℕ) (hsr : s ≤ r)
    (hM : Nonempty (M ≅ SheafOfModules.free
      (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin s))))
    (hN : Nonempty (N ≅ SheafOfModules.free
      (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin n)))) :
    ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X),
      IsClosedImmersion i ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation i ∧
      (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (h : T ⟶ X),
        (∃ g : T ⟶ Z, g ≫ i = h) ↔
          SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
            (kernel ((Modules.pullback h).map d)) r)
